author: Jardine & Selby, 1828

art.subject: Bulwer's Petrel (Bulweria bulwerii), adult: entire plumage dark sooty brown-black, slightly paler and browner on the chin and throat; a pale grey-brown diagonal bar across the upperwing coverts from the wrist towards the body, contrasting with the blackish flight feathers; underwing uniformly dark; long tail blackish-brown, usually closed to a point. Bill short, stout and black; iris dark.
art.pose: flying low over the sea with wings bowed and tail closed to a point, side view
art.scene: open subtropical sea in summer far off southern Korea, bright sky over blue water; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small, slim, all-dark petrel, much smaller than Streaked Shearwater but clearly larger than a storm petrel. Small round head and short neck. Bill short, black, thick, with tube nostrils and a hooked tip. Wings long and narrow, held slightly forward and bowed, with a distinct bend at the wrist. Tail long and wedge-shaped, usually held closed into a long point, giving a long-rear look. Flight buoyant and erratic, low over the waves, twisting with short glides.
avoid: Do not make the tail short or square; it is long and wedge-shaped, usually closed into a point.
Do not paint it like Swinhoe's Storm Petrel, which is much smaller with a forked tail.
Do not show white underparts, a white rump or a white face; it is entirely dark.
Do not paint a long thin shearwater bill; it is short and thick.
